content:
Fox News personality Harris Faulkner had a blunt message for people excited about playing “Grand Theft Auto VI”: “Get back to work.”

The popular and violent video game franchise just released its sixth edition after a 13-year break. Some experts suggested the game might cost U.S. businesses millions in lost productivity from Americans taking PTO to play it.

On Thursday’s episode of “Outnumbered,” Faulkner admitted to hating the possibility that American workers might shirk their duties to corporate overlords by ― oh no! ― staying home to play a video game.

In fact, her response to that possibility had real “get off my lawn” energy.

Faulkner said fans considering skipping work to play “GTA” have no right to gripe about things like higher prices.

“If this generation wants to preach about affordability, but they’re willing to cost billions of dollars in revenue loss on a day like today to go play a game, that probably tells you everything you need to know about what we need to be talking with this younger generation about,” she said, before admonishing these lazy scofflaws to “be a good shepherd of what you have. It may not be there tomorrow.”

She finished her diatribe by telling “GTA” fans: “Get yourself to work.”

On Wednesday, Rachel Campos-Duffy was accused of “culture war bullshit” after she declared, “I’m not thinking this is a good thing for our culture and society.”

On Thursday, Florida Sen. Ashley Moody was brutally mocked after she griped that the game made the Sunshine State seem more lawless than she claimed it really was.

But the reaction to Faulkner was on another level, with many people noting that her comment seemed to attack young adult males, a demographic the Republican Party desperately needs if it wants success in coming elections.
